ID: `impeccable`.

## What it does

Loads product context, visual direction and the surface brief, then selects the relevant procedure: design, critique, audit, polish, clarification, adaptation or other work. Distinguishes refinement that preserves identity from a redesign that replaces it. Follows command instructions and, before changing UI, the minimum quality bar. Limits visual verification and corrections to defined passes.

## When to use it

Use it to create a surface, redesign it or address a UI problem with a specific outcome. shape helps define UX/UI before code; critique evaluates design; audit examines technical quality; polish completes an approved direction. It is not needed for backend-only work.

## How to use it

Ask for it by name, or invoke it with `/impeccable` in Claude Code or `$impeccable` in Codex. Specify the surface, goal, constraints and reference material. Name the command if you know it, or describe the need. Request adherence to the brief and project components, with final visual verification and stated limitations.

## What it delivers

- Outcome defined by the selected command
- Any changes to UI or design documents
- Visual evidence and relevant checks

## Example

Use impeccable clarify on the invitation form: make labels and errors understandable while preserving layout, functionality and the product glossary.

## Prerequisites

- The procedure uses the launcher included in the skill and the command references. If the launcher fails, context must be read from existing documents; the failure is declared.
